title: What If You Could See The Words People Swallow?

shots.line: Your mom slides the toast across the table.
shots.scene: Kitchen: Mom slides the toast across the table to Eli
Close on Mom — she smiles, "Eat up..."
Eli looks up; Mom waves — "it's a good day"

shots.line: But above her head, grey words float.
shots.scene: But above her head, grey words float — a faint "I'M SORRY..." appears
The full line, bright grey above Mom
You watch them fade — Eli's eyes follow the words down

shots.line: She never says them. She never will.
shots.scene: She never says them. She never will — Mom turns away to the counter
What is she sorry for? — Eli walks past the station, thinking

shots.line: She missed your game last Tuesday.
shots.scene: She missed your game last Tuesday — Eli keeps walking, head down
She was working late — Eli slows, stops, looks up at the school gate

shots.line: Six days she has carried it.
shots.scene: Six days she has carried it — Eli walks the school hallway
And now it is gone — Eli stops; a faint grey wisp dissolves into smoke

shots.line: Your name is Eli. You are sixteen.
shots.scene: Name card on the void: ELI, 16 YEARS OLD

shots.line: And you can see the words people swallow.
shots.scene: And you can see the words people swallow — Eli at the front, grey words above three students
Every unsaid sentence floats — wide classroom, words above students
— above their head: closer on June and Theo
Grey text. Soft — close on June drawing birds; her grey words hang soft
Like smoke — the words drift up like smoke

shots.line: It hangs for a few seconds. Then it fades.
shots.scene: It hangs for a few seconds. Then it fades — Theo's word goes first, June's follows
RULE CARD — Once a word fades,
RULE CARD — it is gone forever.

shots.line: You cannot make anyone say them.
shots.scene: You cannot make anyone say them — Eli reaches for June's grey word; his hand passes through
You can only watch... — Eli alone in the void; grey words drift past

shots.line: You can watch a whole life...
shots.scene: You can watch a whole life... — a row of grey words fades in above Eli
disappear in grey letters — the row of words melts away; Eli reaches for the last one
Once, just once, you — Eli watches a girl across the schoolyard
— saw a word turn gold: the girl and her friend walk on, the grey word hanging

shots.line: A girl told her friend she was sorry.
shots.scene: A girl told her friend she was sorry — the girl STOPS and turns to her friend
The grey word turned gold — at 1.20 s the grey word turns GOLD
— and floated up, like light: a golden glow keeps rising where it was

shots.line: So what if you could see the words people swallow?
shots.scene: TITLE CARD — So what if you could see the words people swallow? (slow push-in)
CHAPTER PAUSE 1 — the title card holds in silence (music only)

shots.line: At school, Mr. Hale points at the board.
shots.scene: At school, Mr. Hale points at the board
His red pen shakes — close on Hale, the pen trembling

shots.line: Above his head: "I'M AFRAID OF LOSING MY JOB."
shots.scene: Above his head: "I'M AFRAID OF LOSING MY JOB."
He says: Detention — Hale stern, the class flinches

shots.line: Cole shoves a kid in the hallway.
shots.scene: Cole shoves a kid in the hallway
Everyone laughs — the hallway crowd laughs

shots.line: Above his head: "MY DAD HITS ME."
shots.scene: Above his head: "MY DAD HITS ME." — the laughter dies

shots.line: Do you tell him? You don't.
shots.scene: Do you tell him? You don't — Eli close, looking at Cole, shaking his head
Nobody laughs at that — wide hallway, silence
June sits two rows ahead — populated classroom, June at her desk

shots.line: She draws birds in her notebook.
shots.scene: She draws birds in her notebook — close on June's pencil birds
Above her head: "I LIKE YOU."

shots.line: Do you tell her you saw it? You don't.
shots.scene: Do you tell her you saw it? You don't — Eli, torn
She never looks back — June draws on, back to Eli

shots.line: Theo, your best friend since you were six,
shots.scene: Theo, your best friend since you were six, — Theo grins at Eli
— cracks a joke: Theo throws his arms wide
Everyone laughs

shots.line: Above his head: "I MISS MY MOM."
shots.scene: Above his head: "I MISS MY MOM."

shots.line: His mom moved away. He never talks about it.
shots.scene: His mom moved away. He never talks about it — Theo quiet on the bench
You stop laughing — Eli stops; the others are still laughing behind him

shots.line: On the bus, a man sits beside his wife.
shots.scene: On the bus, a man sits beside his wife

shots.line: Above his head: "I DON'T LOVE YOU ANYMORE."
shots.scene: Above his head: "I DON'T LOVE YOU ANYMORE."
It fades... he swallows it — the words dissolve above the bus man

shots.line: She never knows. You feel sick.
shots.scene: She never knows. You feel sick — the wife smiles, unaware; Eli feels sick

shots.line: At lunch, you count the words.
shots.scene: At lunch, you count the words — Eli counts on his fingers at the lunch table
How many today? Forty-three — the 43-word count-up infographic
All gone by dinner — grey words above three lunch students, fading

shots.line: You stop talking to people. Why bother?
shots.scene: You stop talking to people. Why bother? — Eli silent on the sofa at home

shots.line: You already know what they won't say.
shots.scene: You already know what they won't say — in Mr. Hale's office, Hale talks; Eli already knows
You sit alone — wide library, Eli alone at the big table
You carry a notebook — Eli on the roof at sunset, notebook under his arm

shots.line: You write down every word you see.
shots.scene: You write down every word you see — Eli writes at his desk

shots.line: The apology your mom never gave.
shots.scene: The apology your mom never gave — close on the notebook page

shots.line: The thank you your neighbour never said.
shots.scene: The thank you your neighbour never said — a neighbour waves, her word hangs

shots.line: The confession your best friend never made.
shots.scene: The confession your best friend never made — Theo's word over the park bench

shots.line: You tell yourself you are preserving them.
shots.scene: You tell yourself you are preserving them — Eli writes, pages stacking up

shots.line: You are not. You are just watching them disappear.
shots.scene: You are not. You are just watching them disappear — Eli stops; the words on the pages fade
The notebook grows thick — close on the thick, worn notebook
Your hands shake — close on Eli, his hands trembling

shots.line: One night, you catch yourself in the bathroom mirror.
shots.scene: One night, you catch yourself in the bathroom mirror — Eli approaches the mirror

shots.line: Above YOUR head, grey words float.
shots.scene: Above YOUR head, grey words float — the mirror reflection has words above it
"I'M SORRY." "I'M SCARED." "I LOVE YOU." — the stack of Eli's own words
Dozens of them. Stacked. Fading — the stack melts from the top down

shots.line: You have been swallowing your own words... for years.
shots.scene: You have been swallowing your own words... for years — Eli stares at his reflection
And nobody can see them — the reflection alone in the mirror
Except you... in the mirror — Eli touches the mirror; the reflection reaches back
The rule was never one-sided — Eli realises

shots.line: You were just the last to know.
shots.scene: You were just the last to know — Eli, determined, in the mirror
CHAPTER PAUSE 2 — "THE RULE WAS NEVER ONE-SIDED." holds in silence (music only)

shots.line: Your dad comes home at midnight.
shots.scene: Your dad comes home at midnight — Dad walks in, Eli at the table
Warehouse nights — close on Dad, tired in his work shirt
He opens the fridge — the fridge light spills out
He looks at you — Dad turns from the fridge
How was school? Fine — Dad asks; Eli answers short

shots.line: Above his head, the same words as always:
shots.scene: Above his head, the same words as always: — the grey words appear
"I'M PROUD OF YOU, SON." — the full line, bright grey above Dad

shots.line: You have seen them a hundred times.
shots.scene: You have seen them a hundred times — the words hang; Eli has seen them forever
He has never said them — Dad turns away from the table
Not once. Not ever — the words are gone; Dad is at the counter

shots.line: Can you make him say it? No.
shots.scene: Can you make him say it? No — Eli close, shaking his head
That's the rule — the rule, small and gold, between them
So you swallow yours too — Eli at the mirror again, at night
"DAD, I FORGIVE YOU." — Eli's own words in the mirror

shots.line: It floats above your head in the mirror. And fades.
shots.scene: It floats above your head in the mirror. And fades — the words melt away

shots.line: Then Grandma Rose goes to the hospital.
shots.scene: Then Grandma Rose goes to the hospital — Eli walks the corridor
Eighty-two — Grandma Rose, 82 years old
The kindest person you know — Grandma smiles at Eli
You visit her — Eli comes to her bedside
Tubes. Machines — close on the machines beside her bed
Her eyes are closed — close on Grandma's sleeping face

shots.line: Above her head, grey words float.
shots.scene: Above her head, grey words float — faint grey words appear above Grandma
Slow... fading — Grandma's words fade slowly
"TELL YOUR FATHER — the first half of her last words
I LOVE HIM." — the full line, bright grey above Grandma

shots.line: What does she want to say?
shots.scene: What does she want to say? — Eli close, thinking

shots.line: She wants Dad to know... before it is too late.
shots.scene: She wants Dad to know... before it is too late — Eli looks out the window

shots.line: Dad is in the parking lot.
shots.scene: Dad is in the parking lot — Dad leans on his car, alone

shots.line: He won't come up. He never comes up.
shots.scene: He won't come up. He never comes up — Dad shakes his head
You run. Down the stairs — Eli sprints down the stairwell
Across the lot. Dad! — Eli sprints across and shouts; Dad turns
You grab his arm — Eli grabs Dad's arm

shots.line: Grandma wants to say she loves you.
shots.scene: Grandma wants to say she loves you — Eli pleads

shots.line: He stares. She can say it herself.
shots.scene: He stares. She can say it herself — Dad stares, disbelieving
No, Dad. She can't — Eli shakes his head, urgent

shots.line: She is trying. And her words are fading.
shots.scene: She is trying. And her words are fading — Eli points up at the hospital
Right now — Eli, urgent, close

shots.line: What if it fades before he gets there?
shots.scene: What if it fades before he gets there? — Dad looks at the hospital

shots.line: He looks at the hospital. He looks at you.
shots.scene: He looks at the hospital. He looks at you — Dad turns from the hospital to Eli
Then he runs — Dad runs for the hospital doors
You follow him up — the lift doors close on Dad and Eli
Room 312 — the door with the number 312
Grandma's eyes open — her eyes flutter open
Dad takes her hand — Dad kneels and takes Grandma's hand
His voice breaks. Mom. — Dad's voice breaks
I love you — Dad says it out loud

shots.line: And above her head, the grey words...
shots.scene: And above her head, the grey words... — the grey words hang above Grandma
turn gold — GOLD: Grandma's grey words turn gold
They rise. Like light — the gold glow keeps rising where the words were
Grandma smiles... I know — she smiles; the gold glow rises (holds through the pause)
CHAPTER PAUSE 3 — the gold glow keeps rising over Grandma in silence (music only)

shots.line: That night, Dad sits on your bed.
shots.scene: That night, Dad sits on your bed
He looks at his hands... — Dad looks down at his hands

shots.line: Eli. I'm proud of you, son.
shots.scene: Eli. I'm proud of you, son — Dad says it, out loud, at last

shots.line: The words he has swallowed for years...
shots.scene: The words he has swallowed for years... — Eli looks above Dad's head: nothing there
finally said. Out loud — Dad smiles; nothing floats above him
Above his head, nothing floats — wide: empty sky above Dad's head

shots.line: Because there is nothing left to swallow.
shots.scene: Because there is nothing left to swallow — Dad and Eli, warm and easy
You look in the mirror — Eli turns to the mirror

shots.line: Above your head: "DAD, I FORGIVE YOU."
shots.scene: Above your head: "DAD, I FORGIVE YOU." — his words wait in the mirror

shots.line: Would you say it? You do.
shots.scene: Would you say it? You do — Eli decides
You turn around... — Eli turns from the mirror toward Dad
Dad. I forgive you — Eli says it to Dad's face

shots.line: The words turn gold. They rise.
shots.scene: The words turn gold. They rise — GOLD: Eli's words turn gold and rise like light

shots.line: The next day, you tell June.
shots.scene: The next day, you tell June — Eli and June walk in the park
I like you. She blushes — Eli says it; close on June, blushing

shots.line: I know. I swallowed it too.
shots.scene: I know. I swallowed it too — June smiles; she swallowed it too
You tell Theo — Eli finds Theo in the gym
I miss your mom too — Eli says it to Theo
He cries... he laughs — Theo cries, then laughs
You start saying everything — Eli walks through the school gate, gold wisps rising
Every word. Before it fades — Eli waves; small gold words rise around him
Is any of this real? — Eli asks the question on the void

shots.line: The words are fiction. The swallowing is not.
shots.scene: The words are fiction. The swallowing is not — the answer, in two lines

shots.line: Daniel Wegner at Harvard studied thought suppression.
shots.scene: Daniel Wegner at Harvard studied thought suppression — FREEZE: the white-bear lab

shots.line: He found that trying not to think about something
shots.scene: He found that trying not to think about something — the bear waits
— makes it come back stronger: the comeback arrow circles the bear

shots.line: What you swallow does not vanish.
shots.scene: What you swallow does not vanish — the bear waits
It waits — the white bear, waiting in the dark

shots.line: Psychologists Thomas Gilovich and Victoria Medvec found
shots.scene: Psychologists Thomas Gilovich and Victoria Medvec found — FREEZE: the regret study
that in the long run... — the two empty bars wait on the axes

shots.line: people regret the things they did NOT do...
shots.scene: ...people regret the things they did NOT do — the two bars grow: inactions tower over actions

shots.line: far more than the things they did.
shots.scene: far more than the things they did — the INACTIONS bar glows gold

shots.line: The words they did not say.
shots.scene: The words they did not say — grey unsaid words drift and fade

shots.line: The chances they did not take.
shots.scene: The chances they did not take — the second line fades too

shots.scene: Nurse Bronnie Ware spent years with dying people — her portrait card

shots.scene: I wish I'd lived a life true to myself — regret #1, full line

shots.scene: Number four: I wish I'd stayed in touch with friends — regret #4

— six thousand thoughts a day: the full 6,000-dot infographic

shots.scene: How many of them do you say out loud? — only a few dots turn gold

shots.line: How many fade... before anyone hears them?
shots.scene: How many fade... before anyone hears them? — the grey dots fade away
Next morning. The bus — Eli waits; the bus pulls in

shots.scene: A stranger sits across from you

shots.scene: Above her head, one grey word floats — a single grey word appears
"GOODBYE." — the word, big and close

You stand up... — Eli stands
What do you do? — Eli looks straight at the viewer
What words have you swallowed? — the question, in gold

Tell us in the comments — the comment CTA
